Marcus —

Thanks for the chat earlier. We’re starting our renewal discussions for our contract that expires in late July. A couple of asks from our side:

- We need EU onshore deployment as the primary residency for all PHI traffic by Q4.
- We want APAC to be configured as a warm-standby for bursting and DR, with capacity to handle a 2x spike for up to 72 hours.
- Any changes to term length or billing model we should be aware of for this geography change?

Can you propose a staging approach that minimizes downtime and an estimate for the uplift in committed capacity and costs? I’ve attached our internal timeline (Novacare-MAP-v2.xlsx).

Best,

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the timeline and the context. We can support the EU onshore primary residency with APAC as a warm-standby. High-level proposal below; I’ve attached a draft SOW with a capacity appendix for APAC: SOW-Redline-v1.pdf, Capacity-Appendix-APAC.csv.

Proposed staging (minimal downtime):
1) Phase A (30 days): Provision EU dedicated tenants, run mirror sync for non-PII workloads and validate parity.
2) Phase B (14 days): Route a subset (10-20%) of production traffic to EU for validation; enable prefix/KV cache warmup.
3) Phase C (7 days): Full cutover to EU primary; APAC remains warm-standby with auto-burst policy (2x baseline for 72h).

Commercial/term notes:
- Recommend a 12-month renewal with a 6-month committed capacity uplift for APAC (to reserve warm-standby). We can offer a 10% discount on committed APAC capacity if signed before 2027-07-15.
- Bill for onshore EU residency includes a small data egress premium and an isolation premium per tenant. I’ll include line items in the SOW.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Grace for migration runbook details and Ben for pricing/commits. If you agree, I’ll send a clean SOW and a version for your legal team with redlines inline.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead — Redwood Inference

Emma —

Quick technical follow-ups from our infra team (copied below):

- We recommend a staged cache-warmup strategy tied to prefix lengths to keep tail latency stable. For the 10–20% validation traffic, we’ll use continuous batching policies with a max latency SLO of 150ms.
- For APAC warm-standby, do you prefer a hot-warm model (sharded KV caches kept warm) or cold-warm (KV rebuild on failover)? Hot-warm will increase committed GPU hours by ~35% but reduce failover RTO to under 10 minutes.
- Our suggested runbook step for cutover includes a pre-cut health check and a rollback window of 60 minutes post-cut.

Ben — can you confirm delta pricing for hot-warm vs cold-warm and update the attached SOW appendix? Emma — if you have a preference, call it out and we’ll reflect it in the price table.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
